grammar_function: A place; It is a/an place. Action in a place (in the park).

title: 2.2 Streets and Transportation
new_vocabulary: street; bridge; bus; car; bike

title: 2.6 Numbers 1-5

title: 2.7 Numbers 6-10
new_vocabulary: six; seven; eight; nine; ten
grammar_function: Number words; What number is it? / It is number + number for all ten numeral cards; number + plural noun.

title: 2.8 Basic Colors
new_vocabulary: color; red; blue; green; yellow; black; white
grammar_function: What color is it? / What color are they?; It is + color; They are + color; a + color + noun.

title: 2.9 Count and Describe
new_vocabulary: books; pens; phones; bags; cars
grammar_function: English adjective order number + color + noun; singular after one and regular plural -s after two or more. No There are yet.

title: 2.10 These and Those
new_vocabulary: these; those; which one
grammar_function: These/those + are + plural noun, beside this/that + is + a + noun; Which one? The + color + one.

title: 2.11 Unit 2 Review
grammar_function: Mixed What is it?, It is..., This/That is..., and number-color-noun phrases.

title: 2.12 Encuentro en el parque
grammar_function: What is it? / It is a...; This is... / That is...; numbers 1–10; number + color + singular/plural noun.

title: 3.1 Greetings and Names
new_vocabulary: hello; good morning; goodbye; What is your name?; My name is...
grammar_function: My and your are learned only inside the fixed name chunks; possessive substitution waits for 3.10.

title: 3.2 I, You, and We
new_vocabulary: I; you; we; am
grammar_function: I am; you are; we are. Speaker perspective is shown explicitly, not inferred from a third-person picture.

title: 3.3 Am, Is, and Are
new_vocabulary: doing; What are you doing?
grammar_function: What are you doing? / I am ...; What is she doing? / She is ...; What is he doing? / He is ...; What are they doing? / They are ... . Complete present-progressive exchanges using familiar Unit 1 actions; do/does is not generalized.

title: 3.4 Yes and No
new_vocabulary: yes; no; Are you...?; Is he...?; Is she...?
grammar_function: Be before the subject for a yes/no question; short answers Yes, he is. / No, she is not. / Yes, I am.

title: 3.5 Ages 11-15
new_vocabulary: eleven; twelve; thirteen; fourteen; fifteen; How old are you?; years old
grammar_function: How old are you? / How old is he/she? He/She is + number + years old. What number is it? It is number...

title: 3.6 Ages 16-20
new_vocabulary: sixteen; seventeen; eighteen; nineteen; twenty
grammar_function: How old are you? I am + number + years old. How old is he/she? Is she sixteen? Yes, she is.

title: 3.7 Where Are You From?
new_vocabulary: Mexico; Mexican; the United States; American; from; Where are you from?
grammar_function: Where are you from? I am from + country. I am + nationality. Where is a fixed origin chunk.

title: 3.8 Canada and Spain
new_vocabulary: Canada; Canadian; Spain; Spanish
grammar_function: Where are you from? / Where is he/she from? He/She is from + country. I am + nationality.

title: 3.9 Professions
new_vocabulary: teacher; doctor; cook; driver; farmer; nurse; job; What is your job?
grammar_function: What is your job? I am a + job. He/She is a + job. Is he a driver? No, he is not.

title: 3.10 My, Your, His, and Her
new_vocabulary: my; your; his; her
grammar_function: Possessive adjective + noun: my/your/his/her name or object.

title: 3.11 Our and Their
new_vocabulary: our; their
grammar_function: Our/their + familiar singular or plural noun; the speaker is included only in our.

new_vocabulary: have; has; mine; yours; ours
grammar_function: He/she has; I/you/we/they have. This car is mine. This book is yours. That house is ours. Is this phone yours?

title: 3.13 Unit 3 Review
grammar_function: Hello/Good morning/Goodbye; What is your name? My name is...; I am/you are/we are; What are you doing? I am + -ing; How old are you? I am ... years old; Where are you from? I am from... / I am + nationality; What is your job? I am a...; he/she is; my/your/his/her; have/has. Is she cooking? Yes, she is.; our/their; It is yours. Name objects explicitly; That house is ours. Is this phone yours? Yes, this phone is mine.

title: 3.14 Cenas cruzadas
grammar_function: Hello/Good morning/Goodbye; What is your name? My name is...; I am/you are/we are; he/she is, they are; What are you doing? title: 4.1 Rooms at Home
new_vocabulary: home; kitchen; bedroom; bathroom; living room; dining room
grammar_function: This is the + room. The grandmother is in the kitchen. The adults are in the living room.

title: 4.2 Furniture and Home Objects
new_vocabulary: bed; sofa; lamp; door; window; computer
grammar_function: It is a + noun. The bed is in the bedroom. Is it a door? Yes, it is. / No, it is not.

title: 4.3 Where Things Are
new_vocabulary: in; on; under; next to; Where is
grammar_function: Where is the + named object? The named object is in/on/under/next to the + known noun.

title: 4.4 There Is and There Are
new_vocabulary: there is; there are
grammar_function: There is + a + singular noun; there are + number + plural noun; a location phrase from 4.3.

title: 4.5 Morning Routine
new_vocabulary: wake up; wash my face; brush my teeth; eat breakfast; get dressed; in the morning
grammar_function: I + routine chunk as a learned whole; + in the + room; + in the morning.

title: 4.6 Getting ready for school day routine
new_vocabulary: first; then; after that; finally; go to school
grammar_function: Describe getting ready for school in order with first, then, after that and finally.

title: 4.7 Helping at home
new_vocabulary: open; close; clothes; clean
grammar_function: Describe opening and closing a door, washing clothes, and cleaning a table with meaningful I, you, we and they perspectives. Reuse familiar home objects and rooms.

title: 4.8 Do you...? Questions and replies
new_vocabulary: Do you...?; Yes, I do.; No, I do not.; work; study; play; run
grammar_function: Ask with Do + you + action? Respond with Yes, I do. or No, I do not. Keep the question auxiliary central while practising familiar actions and places.

title: 4.9 Days of the Week
new_vocabulary: Monday; Tuesday; Wednesday; Thursday; Friday; Saturday; Sunday; What day is it today?
grammar_function: What day is it today? Today is + day.

title: 4.10 What Time Is It?
new_vocabulary: What time is it?; o'clock; afternoon; evening; night; at; a.m.; p.m.
grammar_function: It is morning/afternoon/evening/night; What time is it? It is + number + o'clock; in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening / at night; It is + number + a.m./p.m. No routines or activity-at-time statements.

title: 4.11 Unit 4 Review — Home, help and plans
grammar_function: Bring the whole unit together: rooms and objects, named-object locations, morning order, helping at home, Do you...? questions and replies, days and times. Fresh scenes; no new English.

title: 4.12 Un día en casa — A family visit
grammar_function: Known home/location, school sequence and household action language; auxiliary Do with both short replies; weekday and whole-hour time.

title: 5.1 Fruits
new_vocabulary: fruit; apple; banana; orange; grapes; strawberry; pear
grammar_function: a/an + fruit; It is a pear. They are grapes. The apple is green. Three oranges. The baby is eating a banana.

title: 5.2 Food
new_vocabulary: food; bread; rice; egg; chicken; fish
grammar_function: It is bread. The boy is eating rice. The father is cooking fish. There are three eggs.

title: 5.3 Drinks
new_vocabulary: drinks; water; milk; juice; coffee; tea; drink
grammar_function: The grandmother is drinking tea. I drink water in the morning. Do you drink coffee? Yes, I do.

title: 5.4 How Many? and Some
new_vocabulary: How many...?; some
grammar_function: How many + plural noun + are there? There are three apples. There is some rice.

title: 5.5 Likes, Dislikes, and Agreement
new_vocabulary: like; do not like; Me too.; Me neither.
grammar_function: I like coffee. Me too. I do not like milk. Me neither. Do you like coffee? Yes, I do.

title: 5.6 Wants and Needs
new_vocabulary: want; do not want; need; do not need; wants; needs
grammar_function: I want juice. I do not want milk. I need water. I do not need juice. He wants bread. She needs milk. They want chicken. They need some water.

title: 5.7 Meals
new_vocabulary: lunch; dinner; for
grammar_function: I eat eggs for breakfast. They eat chicken for dinner. They eat lunch at one o'clock.

title: 5.8 Prices
new_vocabulary: How much is...?; dollar; dollars
grammar_function: How much is the bread? The bread is five dollars. How much is the milk? The milk is two dollars.

title: 5.9 Ordering Politely 1: At a Café
new_vocabulary: How can I help you?; Can I have...?; please; Here is your...; Here are your...; Here you are.; Thank you.
grammar_function: Hello! How can I help you? Can I have coffee, please? Here is your coffee. Thank you. Can I have coffee and eggs, please? Here are your coffee and eggs.

title: 5.10 Ordering Politely 2: At the Market and Shops
new_vocabulary: Yes, please.; No, thank you.
grammar_function: Can I have three apples, please? Here are your three apples. Do you want a bag? Yes, please. No, thank you. Can I have the blue bag, please? How much is the bag?

title: 5.11 Unit 5 Review
grammar_function: Spiral review of there is/there are, How many ... are there?, some, like and do not like, Me too, want and need, meals with for, prices with dollars, and Can I have ..., please?

title: 5.12 Un día en el mercado y el café
grammar_function: Integrate food wants/needs, purchasing actions, and polite requests.

title: 6.1 Places Around Town
new_vocabulary: station; bank; pharmacy; library; mall; supermarket
grammar_function: Ana and her family make a short neighborhood visit. Start at the station, locate the father at the bank and the mother at the pharmacy, find the children at the library, then meet at the mall and get food at the supermarket. Explicit Spanish transitions explain each change of location; the English stays within the early lesson’s scope.

title: 6.2 Ways to Travel
new_vocabulary: train; taxi; airplane; boat; walk; by
grammar_function: Begin with a familiar school journey by bus. Compare train and taxi for the town visit, then walking for a nearby library. A clearly introduced second travel situation extends the same pattern to an airplane and a boat; it is not a magical bus–plane–boat trip.

title: 6.3 Where Are You Going?
new_vocabulary: going
grammar_function: Ana is leaving for the mall. Luis asks her destination. They then talk about a man going to the bank and a woman going to the library. Finally, Ana’s family joins her: we are going to the mall, while an outside observer describes the same group as they. Every question is followed by the answer it requests.

title: 6.4 More Places to Visit
new_vocabulary: hotel; post office; museum; movie theater; bus stop; airport
grammar_function: Visitors start at their hotel. The family’s outing is the museum, with a post office and movie theater located nearby. Find the bus stop for that outing. A clearly announced later journey connects the hotel, taxi and airport; airplane is retrieved as the reason for this travel point.

title: 6.5 A Trip to the Mall
new_vocabulary: get on; get off; get in; get out of
grammar_function: Ana walks to the bus stop, gets on the bus, gets off at the mall, walks inside, requests and receives juice, thanks the clerk, then takes a taxi home and gets out.

title: 6.6 Finding Places in the Neighborhood
new_vocabulary: near; far from; between; across from
grammar_function: Ana wants to find the library from the hotel. Luis first establishes which places are near and far, then pinpoints the library between two landmarks and across from the mall. Ana has enough information to walk to the correct building. Use one stable neighborhood with explicit wide and close views.

title: 6.7 Which Side of the Street?
new_vocabulary: left; right; on the left; on the right
grammar_function: Ana and Luis face the same direction from the hotel entrance. The mall is on their left and the pharmacy on their right. Ana is going to the mall; she confirms the side and finds the entrance. After arrival, a clearly marked second viewpoint introduces the station and the bank without silently reversing left and right.

title: 6.8 Following Directions
new_vocabulary: go straight; turn left; turn right; cross the street; stop; corner; go past
grammar_function: Luis gives Ana a route from the hotel to the museum: go straight, go past the bank, turn left at the corner, cross at the reviewed crossing and stop at the museum. Ana follows it. Only after this route ends does a short, explicitly separate route to the movie theater practise turn right.

title: 6.9 Finding a Safe Way
new_vocabulary: can; cannot; here; there
grammar_function: Ana’s first crossing is unavailable. A clearly pictured signal or barrier establishes why she cannot cross here. Luis indicates an available crossing there. Ana follows the short known route, crosses only where permitted, and continues to the museum.

title: 6.10 Can You Help Me Get There?
new_vocabulary: Excuse me; Can you help me; Sorry, no; How do I get to
grammar_function: Ana is going to the mall but needs directions. She approaches one person, asks for help and hears Sorry, no. A clear transition introduces Luis as a different helper. He agrees, hears the named destination, gives a usable route, receives thanks, and Ana follows the route to the mall. This is where the fuller story and conversation belong.

title: 6.11 Which Bus Do I Need?
new_vocabulary: ticket; take; goes; Which bus; next stop
grammar_function: Ana is going to the museum. Luis identifies the right bus. At the counter Ana asks for a ticket and its price; the clerk hands it over and she thanks the clerk. She boards the identified bus, hears the next stop, gets off, and completes the walk to the museum.

title: 6.12 What Time Does It Leave?
new_vocabulary: leaves; arrives; What time does; leave; arrive
grammar_function: Ana checks a train journey from the station to the museum area. The train leaves at nine in the morning and arrives at ten. She asks both questions, obtains her ticket, boards before departure, then gets off after arrival. A clearly separate return service is introduced only after this journey ends.

title: 6.13 Three Trips Around Town
grammar_function: Three fresh transfer trips: family boat to mall/supermarket and taxi to hotel; asking different helpers, taking the blue bus and following safe walking directions to the museum; checking train times, buying and receiving a ticket, reaching the airport and boarding an airplane.

title: 6.14 Mission: Meet at the Museum
grammar_function: Current destinations, a help exchange, safe directions, service choice, a ticket transaction, schedules and a complete trip.

title: 7.1 My Body
new_vocabulary: head; eyes; ears; nose; mouth; arms; hands; fingers; legs; feet; toes
grammar_function: A continuous head-to-toe sequence; This is my ... and I have two/ten ... with Sofía as the first-person speaker.

title: 7.2 How Are You?
new_vocabulary: happy; sad; tired; hungry; thirsty; How are you?; How is she?; How is the grandfather?; How is the baby?
grammar_function: How are you / How is she / How is the grandfather / How is the baby; feeling, need, request, handover and thanks.

title: 7.3 My Clothes
new_vocabulary: shirt; pants; dress; skirt; jacket; hat; socks; shoes
grammar_function: Name clothes, identify colors and describe the clothing of an explicitly established owner.

title: 7.4 The Weather Today
new_vocabulary: sunny; cloudy; rainy; windy; cold; hot; How is the weather today?
grammar_function: Ask How is the weather today? and describe the explicitly introduced day or place.

title: 7.5 Clothes for the Weather
new_vocabulary: coat; sweater; scarf; gloves; umbrella; boots; shorts
grammar_function: Name weather clothes, state an explicit need and locate belongings.

title: 7.6 What I Like to Do
new_vocabulary: I like to; Do you like to; watch TV; listen to music; dance; draw; paint; ride a bike; take photos; play football
grammar_function: Explicit I like to preferences and Do you like to questions with eight activities; pictures identify an activity, never a hidden opinion.

title: 7.7 Let's Do Something Together
new_vocabulary: Do you want to; Let's; OK; read
grammar_function: Invite with Do you want to and Let's; accept, decline and offer another activity.

title: 7.8 Please Repeat
new_vocabulary: I do not understand; Please repeat; fast; Please speak slowly
grammar_function: Identify a communication problem, request repetition or clearer speech, confirm unchanged information and reach the destination.

title: 7.9 Three Everyday Situations
grammar_function: Retrieve Unit 7 language in three fresh, coherent everyday situations.

title: 7.10 Un día con amigos
grammar_function: Apply previously taught A1 language throughout a coherent outing.

title: 1.1 What people look like
new_vocabulary: tall; short; long hair; beard; old; young
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.1 Meet the People: He is a man. becomes He is an old man. It adds no new grammar relationship: be + a description (Luis is tall.), has + a feature (A1 3.12 has: Diego has a beard.) and a/an before a description (an old man).

title: 1.2 What people do
new_vocabulary: drinks; reads; writes; eats
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.2 People in Action: He is eating. becomes He eats fruit. The one new grammar relationship is he/she + verb + -s (A1 has it only for wants/needs), taught as the contrast I drink coffee. / Luis drinks coffee. and heard against A1's is ...-ing.

title: 1.3 What they do
new_vocabulary: swim; swims; runs
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.3 Two People: They and Are: They are swimming. becomes They swim. The one new grammar relationship is they/we + verb without -s, taught as the contrast They swim. / Ana swims. after 1.2's he/she -s.

title: 1.4 Where my family lives
new_vocabulary: aunt; uncle; cousin; lives in; with
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.4-1.6: the family grows to aunt, uncle and cousin. It adds no new grammar relationship: 1.2's he/she -s returns on a new verb, lives (My aunt lives in Canada. She lives in Canada.), with A1's countries and lives with + a known family word.

title: 1.5 Brothers and sisters
new_vocabulary: do you have; older; younger
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.5 Brothers, Sisters and Adults: brothers and sisters become a question. The one new grammar relationship is the question frame How many + family word + do you have?, built from A1's How many ...? (How many apples are there?) and Do you ...? (Do you work?), answered with A1's I have. Older and younger grow A1+ 1.1's old and young into family words, with A1 1.5's an before older (an older sister). Has returns with names (Ana has two sisters.).

title: 1.6 How often my family does it
new_vocabulary: always; usually; sometimes; never
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.6 Parents and Grandparents: the family words return with how often each person does something. The one new grammar relationship is the frequency word between the person and the verb (My grandmother always drinks tea.), on A1+ 1.2's he/she -s and 1.3's runs in the park.

title: 1.7 How often do you study?
new_vocabulary: How often; studies; works
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.7 Family Actions: studying and working become habits. The one new grammar relationship is the question How often + do you + verb?, built from A1 4.8's Do you study? and answered with A1+ 1.6's frequency words before the verb (I usually study at night.). The report uses A1+ 1.2's he/she -s, where study takes the -ies spelling (studies) and work the plain -s (works).

title: 1.8 Ask for the information that is missing
new_vocabulary: Where; When
grammar_function: The learner selects the kind of missing information instead of repeating a preset question. The response changes the arrangement or identifies the right person.

title: 1.9 Give a reason and suggest a workable alternative
new_vocabulary: Why; because
grammar_function: An alternative must address the reason. The learner follows a cause-and-response chain instead of recognizing a polite refusal.

title: 1.10 The usual plan has changed today
grammar_function: Use changed information to revise an earlier plan, preserving which fact is usual and which is true today.

title: 1.11 Review: three people, one workable arrangement
grammar_function: Transfer the unit’s tools to new combinations and identify the relevant follow-up without a new-language load.

title: 1.12 Mission: make the visit work
grammar_function: Maintain and update a shared set of facts across an uninterrupted story; resolve the arrangement rather than merely following a route or naming activities.
